findings.title: JUST_LOGGED_UNDO widget flag is never cleared automatically -- once set, the widget shows "Logged just now / Undo" forever instead of the countdown/overdue display
findings.why_it_matters: LogNowAction sets prefs[JUST_LOGGED_UNDO] = true after every widget-tap log. The only other write site for this key anywhere in the app is UndoLogAction, which sets it back to false. There is no timer, no elapsed-time check, and no other code path (WidgetRefreshWorker, BackdateViewModel's onEntrySaved, HistoryViewModel's onEntriesChanged, SettingsViewModel's onIntervalChanged -- all of which just call FeedWidget().updateAll()) that ever resets the flag. FeedWidget.provideGlance() reads the persisted flag unconditionally (`prefs[WidgetActionHandler.JUST_LOGGED_UNDO] ?: false`) and WidgetContent renders the undo overlay instead of the status (NoData/CountdownRemaining/OverdueBy) whenever it is true. Concretely: the father taps "Log feed now" once; from that point forward, every redraw of the widget -- including the 15-minute WidgetRefreshWorker backstop, and redraws triggered by unrelated History edits/deletes or Settings interval changes -- keeps showing "Logged just now" / "Undo" and never again shows the next-feed countdown or overdue indicator (R5/R6/R9), unless the user happens to tap "Undo" (which deletes whatever entry is currently FeedRepository.mostRecent() -- not necessarily the entry originally logged, since further feeds may have been added in the meantime via backdating or History). This directly contradicts the plan's own stated intent that this is a 'brief inline undo affordance ... specifically to cover an accidental double-tap' (Key Technical Decisions) -- the implementation has no mechanism to make it brief. Functionally, this breaks the widget's primary value proposition (R5/R6/R9 display) after the very first tap of its only action (R1).
findings.evidence: app/src/main/java/com/snimesh/baby_feed/widget/LogNowAction.kt:16 sets JUST_LOGGED_UNDO = true; app/src/main/java/com/snimesh/baby_feed/widget/UndoLogAction.kt:14 is the only site that sets it back to false; app/src/main/java/com/snimesh/baby_feed/widget/FeedWidget.kt:32-34 reads the flag with no expiry logic and routes rendering through WidgetContent.kt:28 (`if (state.justLoggedUndo) { ... } else { when (status) { ... } }`). Grep across app/src confirms JUST_LOGGED_UNDO/justLoggedUndo appear in exactly these files plus WidgetUiState.kt (data holder) and WidgetContentTest.kt (which only tests the static rendering of the flag, not its lifecycle/expiry) -- no timer, no WorkManager job, no timestamp comparison anywhere clears it automatically.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sticky boolean with a time-bounded signal: store the timestamp at which JUST_LOGGED_UNDO was set (a Long preference) instead of a plain boolean, and in FeedWidget.provideGlance() (and/or WidgetRefreshWorker) treat it as active only while `System.currentTimeMillis() - loggedAtMillis < UNDO_WINDOW_MILLIS` (e.g. 5-10 seconds), falling back to the normal status display once the window elapses -- clearing the stored preference at that point too so a stale value doesn't linger. Alternatively, schedule a one-shot WorkManager job (or a short coroutine delay inside LogNowAction.onAction, if Glance's ActionCallback execution window allows it) that flips the flag back to false and calls updateAll() a few seconds after logging.

residual_risks: AndroidSpeechCaptureController.startListening()'s RecognitionListener callbacks (onResults/onError) are assumed to run on the thread that created the SpeechRecognizer; this holds as long as startListening() is always invoked from Dispatchers.Main (true today via viewModelScope.launch's default dispatcher), but the assumption is implicit and would silently break (recognizer created/used off the main thread) if a caller ever changed the dispatcher.

MediaPipeTimeParsingLlm.parse()'s lazy `llmInference ?: loadModel().also { llmInference = it }` is not atomic; if parse() were ever called concurrently from two call sites (not currently possible given the single-screen UI gating), both could observe null and load the ~529MB model twice. Already flagged by the performance reviewer; noted here only because it borders on a correctness (double-instance) concern rather than pure performance.

BackdateViewModel.onConfirm() does not catch IllegalArgumentException from repository.logFeed(); currently unreachable because every path into Confirming already validates timestampMillis <= some earlier 'now' snapshot, but this invariant is implicit across three different producers (LLM parse, manual picker offsets, confirm-time revalidation) rather than enforced by a type or a single checkpoint, so a future change to any one of those paths could silently reintroduce a crash. Already flagged by the reliability reviewer at lower confidence; noted here as the correctness angle on the same gap.
testing_gaps: No test (unit, instrumented, or Glance widget test) exercises the JUST_LOGGED_UNDO flag's lifecycle beyond a single static render (WidgetContentTest's justLoggedUndo_rendersUndoAffordanceInsteadOfStatus only proves the overlay renders when the flag is true) -- nothing verifies the flag is ever expected to become false again on its own, which is exactly how this gap went uncaught.

No test drives FeedWidget.provideGlance() end-to-end (real GlanceAppWidget + real persisted Preferences state) across a sequence of actions -- e.g. log now, then wait/advance time, then assert the widget falls back to showing the countdown -- so the full widget state machine (log -> undo-overlay -> countdown) is unverified as a sequence, only its individual pieces are.
